provider_model_version: catalog alias; immutable service snapshot unknown

execution.job_order: manifest order is retained for audit; completion order is not a treatment factor
execution.failure_isolation: Provider or indeterminate transport failure terminates only its job; malformed/truncated candidate output spends its slot and search continues.
execution.data_isolation: Snapshot passed explicitly to pure evaluator; no process-global monkeypatch; separate OS processes.

pool_capacity_rule: When full, evict the worst validation-loss entry with zero outstanding protection slots; preserve its lineage ledger. If every entry has outstanding protected slots, reject the new entry.
direction_identity: Online nearest-linked assignment at fixed probe distance <= 0.08, with stable IDs and no connected-component merge; tags/AST are diagnostics. New mutation directions inherit the parent direction lineage; rejoining an existing direction uses its existing ledger. The cap applies to B-allocated slots, not unlimited incumbent exploitation outside B.
protection_semantics: Both protected and unprotected multi-direction arms receive identical B admission and eligibility grants (2 at a time, 8 per lineage). U uses B on ordinary development slots and may evict entries. P guarantees prompt execution by forcing FIFO B slots and excluding entries with outstanding protected slots from eviction. Invalid proposals spend a slot. No repair/replacement calls. Unredeemable end-of-budget grants are reported separately.

ordinary_scheduling.SP: always develop the current validation incumbent; no branch protection
ordinary_scheduling.WR: always explore with no parent; no branch protection
ordinary_scheduling.FB: Bernoulli 0.5 explore/develop; development selects oldest eligible B entry, else validation incumbent. Both FB_U and FB_P use this identical routine; P additionally forces outstanding protected slots before ordinary scheduling.
ordinary_scheduling.TS: development probability rises linearly from 0.15 to 0.85 over the 32 proposal slots
ordinary_scheduling.AD: select two-proposal units; the first explore and develop units occur in RNG-randomized order; then adapt from global validation-best loss reduction per 1000 actual model tokens using the preregistered normalized difference rule; keep probability in [0.25, 0.75]

adaptive_feedback.initial_order: randomized; one explore unit and one develop unit
adaptive_feedback.reward: Sum of the positive pre/post global-best validation reductions caused by the two ordinary proposals, divided by their combined actual tokens/1000. Intervening forced protection rewards and costs are excluded. This is a direct-reward heuristic; delayed exploration value is not estimated.
adaptive_feedback.estimate: arithmetic mean over all completed units of the same action
adaptive_feedback.missing_usage: Units with unknown actual token usage are omitted from action means; if either action mean is unavailable, p_develop=0.5
adaptive_feedback.protected_slots: Forced protection slots do not increment unit length, unit tokens, or unit reward; they remain part of the job budget and are reported separately
adaptive_feedback.unit_accounting: A unit contains two ordinary proposals, even if protected slots occur between them

comparison_semantics.FB_U: Fully active unprotected B, same eligibility grants, FIFO branch selection, and ordinary routing as FB_P; only priority guarantee and eviction protection differ.
comparison_semantics.FB_P_minus_FB_U: Combined scheduling and eviction protection versus ordinary use of the SAME branch pool; not a separate decomposition of priority and eviction protection.
comparison_semantics.prompt_visibility: The model receives action, parent and reference program facts needed for generation; controller-private probabilities, pool scores, and arm identifiers are retained in audit files and omitted from model prompts.

primary_endpoints: Validation-selected single-program test gap (lower is better)
Paired block-level test-gap difference for FB_P minus FB_U
Paired block-level test-gap differences for TS_P and AD_P versus FB_P
secondary_endpoints: Test-gap improvement versus the best shared hand-written seed
Tokens, requests, wall time, proposal validity and truncation rate
New competitive direction admission, protected-slot scheduling, valid protected evaluations, lagging-parent use and protected local/global improvement

practical_thresholds.interpretation: Decision thresholds are descriptive screening criteria, not a guarantee of confirmatory power.

statistics.paired_blocking: Each arm uses the same generated block and outer random seed; one run per arm per block.
statistics.missing_jobs: All 48 jobs retained. Terminal budget/provider failures with frozen partial output included in primary available-output quality, with failure status and known/unknown cost reported; completion-only contrast is secondary. No-output failures remain missing. No retries/replacements.

failure_policy: Each request is dispatched once. Parse, truncation and invalid-program outcomes consume the proposal slot and actual budget. Indeterminate/provider errors stop that job with no automatic retry. Jobs run independently with bounded parallelism; a failed job does not cancel or replace another job. Test opens only after all planned jobs are terminal.
audit_corrections: The adaptive-unit accounting excludes forced protected slots from proposal count, tokens, and reward.
Lagging-parent status is captured before the protected representative can be updated by the observed candidate.
Controller-private scheduling evidence is not sent to the model.
The preceding r1 execution was halted before test access after these mismatches were found; its three completed searches remain an audit-only archive.
r2 thread-global evaluator interference was confirmed before test evaluation. r2 is excluded from efficacy analysis. r3 uses blocks 32-39 and explicit input evaluation in isolated processes.
The B pool is active in both FB_U and FB_P. The contrast changes minimum-opportunity scheduling and eviction protection, not access to branches.
The direct ordinary AD feedback unit is checked using an interrupted two-proposal synthetic history with intervening protected improvements.
claims: Single-model fixed-budget strategy screening on TSP14. This experiment can estimate whether protected direction development or adaptive scheduling adds value over fixed balance in this task profile. It cannot establish cross-model, cross-task or universal superiority; a later independent confirmatory study is required.
source_output_basis: Use the S1-validated MiniMax M3 caps: planner 16384, coder 8192, temperature 0.7. S1 observed 378/384 valid proposals at these caps; S2's 4000/2400 caps had 78/192 truncated proposals in P1b. New S3 still records its own output outcomes.
readout_policy: Freeze the best validated candidate from completed proposals on every terminal run, including budget exhaustion and provider interruption; evaluate this available-output fallback after all jobs terminate. Show completion-only contrasts as secondary, never silently drop failures. A job with no frozen output stays explicitly missing.
